title: Group Policy Object Modified In The Policies Container
detection_hypothesis: If group policy is used to distribute configuration or execution, the directory change audit will record a write against an object in the policies container.

field_semantics.EventID: Numeric identifier of the Windows event record.
field_semantics.ObjectDN: Distinguished name of the directory object involved in the operation.
field_semantics.OperationType: Type of directory modification, such as value added or deleted.

collection_prerequisites: The relevant advanced audit policy subcategory is enabled for success events.
Domain controller Security logs are forwarded for directory-scoped events.
expected_collection_gaps: Events raised on a domain controller that is not forwarding logs are invisible.
Security log wrapping on busy controllers can drop events before forwarding.
normalization_assumptions: EventID is an integer and Channel is the literal string Security.
Account names are provided without the domain prefix in TargetUserName.
ingestion_differences: Some pipelines rename EventID to event.code or similar.
Directory attribute events may arrive with XML-encoded values.
retention_considerations: Security log volume varies widely; 180 to 365 days is common for identity events.
expected_volume: Low; a handful of matches per change window.
false_positive_strategy: Benign edits come from a known set of policy administrators and correspond to change tickets. Tune by correlating with the change calendar and by watching for edits to policies linked at the domain root.
tuning_guidance: Exclude the baseline tooling service account if its version stamp updates dominate the volume. Keep human-initiated edits visible at all times.
test_strategy: Positive cases modify version and file path attributes on policy objects. Negative cases modify an object outside the container, delete a value, and read the object.

attack_techniques.name: Domain or Tenant Policy Modification: Group Policy Modification

author: Salvatore Mazzaglia
